title: Group operations on a finite normalization over a trait
statement:
Let $V$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $L$ and residue field $k$. Let $G	o\operatorname{Spec}V$ be flat, separated and of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equipped with multiplication $m:G	imes_VG	o G$, identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}V	o G$, and inverse $i:G	o G$ satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams. Let $j:H=G_{\mathrm{red}}	o G$ be the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and let $
u:N	o H$ be the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Assume that $H$ and $N$ are flat, separated and of finite type over $V$, that $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], that $H_L$ is geometrically reduced, and that $N_k$ is geometrically reduced. Geometrically reduced means reduced after every extension of the indicated field, and reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent local sections. The fibres and products are those of [def-pc-base-change]. Then $H$ has a unique $V$-group-scheme structure for which $j$ is a group homomorphism. The map $
u_L:N_L	o H_L$ is an isomorphism, and $N$ has a unique $V$-group-scheme structure for which $
u$ is a homomorphism and $
u_L$ identifies the generic-fibre group structures. A homomorphism here is a morphism commuting with multiplication, identity and inverse. No affineness or connectedness assumption on $G$, and no henselianity, completeness, excellence or perfect-residue-field assumption on $V$, is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/qrg.pdf, Appendix Corollary A.4 proof, printed p.29: reduction subgroup, normality of the product, lifting group law and identity. Normalization universal property: Stacks Tag 035Q, morphisms.tex, lemma-normalization-normal; geometric reduced group smoothness: Tags 047N and 047P, groupoids.tex.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and choose a uniformizer $\pi$. The DVR $V$ is Noetherian, since every ideal is principal. Finite-type schemes over $S$, in particular $H,N$ and their finite fibre powers, are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Their product structure maps are flat: the projections are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and composition is flat on stalks by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. On an affine open of any such flat scheme $X$, its coordinate algebra $A$ is $V$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Tensoring the injection $V\xrightarrow{\pi}V$ with $A$ makes multiplication by $\pi$ injective. The localization zero criterion therefore gives $A\hookrightarrow A[1/\pi]$. In particular, if $X_L$ is reduced then $X$ is reduced: a nilpotent section has zero image in this injective localization. Also $X_L$ is schematically dense in $X$, because the kernel of restriction of the structure sheaf to $X_L$ is zero on this affine cover.

source.place: Appendix A.4 proof, first and third sentences: flat reduction and flat product; elementary uniformizer argument supplied explicitly. Stacks Tags 01T6, 01T3, 01T4, 01U5, 00HC, 00HB and 07JZ.

proof.text: The product $H_L\times_LH_L$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with second factor the geometrically reduced $H_L$ and first factor the reduced Noetherian $H_L$. A module over a field is flat, so the flatness hypothesis holds. Thus step 1 makes $H\times_SH$ reduced. The source $H$ itself is reduced by its definition, and $S$ is reduced since $V$ is a domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to the three maps $m\circ(j\times j)$, $i\circ j$, and $e$. They factor through $j:H\to G$, giving $m_H,i_H,e_H$. A closed immersion is a monomorphism: on affine charts its ring map is surjective, so two maps through it agreeing in $G$ agree in $H$. After composing the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams with $j$ they are the given diagrams for $G$. Monicity proves all diagrams for $H$ and uniqueness of these three operations. Thus $j$ is a homomorphism.

source.place: Appendix Corollary A.4 proof, first paragraph: the reduced product and reduced subgroup; Stacks Tag 0356, schemes.tex, lemma-map-into-reduction.

proof.text:
The finite-type $L$-group $H_L$ is geometrically reduced by hypothesis, hence smooth by [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth]. It is normal by [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], since a field is integrally closed. The inclusion $H_L\hookrightarrow H$ is the open $D(\pi)$ and is smooth: apply [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] with the smooth identity of $H$. Hence [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-smooth-pullback] identifies $N_L	o H_L$ with the componentwise normalization of $H_L$. For any normal scheme $Y$ with locally finite components its normalization is an isomorphism: [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] applied to $\operatorname{id}_Y$ gives a section $s$ of $
u_Y$. The same lemma applied to $
u_Y$ says $s
u_Y=\operatorname{id}$, using normality and the component bijection supplied by [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties]. Apply this to $Y=H_L$. We obtain the asserted isomorphism $
u_L:N_L\simeq H_L$, and give $N_L$ the transported generic group law.

source.place: Appendix Corollary A.4 proof, smooth generic fibre and normalization; Stacks Tags 047N/047P, 034F, 07TD and 035Q(1),(2),(4).

proof.text: Put $P=N\times_SN$. Its generic fibre is $H_L\times_LH_L$ by step 3. This is smooth: on affine charts the projection is the base change of a smooth ring map and the structure map is its composite with a smooth ring map, by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Consequently $P_L$ is normal by [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent]. Its special fibre $P_k=N_k\times_kN_k$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback], since $N_k$ is geometrically reduced and Noetherian. Each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $P$ has $A$ a finitely generated flat $V$-algebra by step 1. Its generic localization is the coordinate ring of an open of $P_L$, hence is normal, and $A/\pi A$ is reduced. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-normal-generic-reduced-special] to $A$. Every such $A$ is normal, so $P$ is normal. Also $N$ is normal by [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties].

source.place: Appendix A.4 proof, third sentence: normality of the normalization product; Remark A.3, Serre criterion. Stacks Tags 00T4, 00TD, 034F and 035Q(1).

proof.text:
We check the component hypothesis for normalization lifting. Every component of a Noetherian flat $S$-scheme meets the generic fibre: locally, its generic point corresponds to a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$; [lem-sc-flat-going-down] applied to $V	o A$ forces $\mathfrak q\cap V=(0)$, since a prime strictly below it cannot exist. The identification of components with minimal primes is [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. By [lem-sc-components-open-injection], intersection with the open generic fibre identifies these components with its components, and closing in the total space recovers them. On the generic fibre, $m_{H,L}:H_L	imes_LH_L	o H_L$ is smooth: $(x,y)\mapsto(xy,y)$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(z,y)\mapsto(zy^{-1},y)$, and multiplication is its first projection. The projection is smooth by the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], hence flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Going down again makes each component dominate a component. Thus $m_H\circ(
u	imes
u):P	o H$ is component-dominant, since $
u_L$ is an isomorphism. The same argument for $i_H
u:N	o H$ is immediate on the generic fibre, where inversion is an isomorphism. Taking closures proves its component dominance as well.

source.place: Appendix A.4 proof, universal property of normalization: verification of its component-dominance hypothesis; Stacks Tags 00HS, 00ES, 00T4 and 01V4.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] to $P	o H$ and $N	o H$ from step 5. Their sources are normal by step 4, and the target is Noetherian by step 1. We obtain unique morphisms $m_N:P	o N$ and $i_N:N	o N$ with $
u m_N=m_H(
u	imes
u)$ and $
u i_N=i_H
u$. Restricting these equations to the generic fibre and composing with $
u_L^{-1}$ shows that they are exactly the multiplication and inverse transported in step 3. No lift of the identity is being inferred from component dominance: a section need not dominate a component.

source.place: Appendix A.4 proof, lifting the generic group law by normalization; Stacks Tag 035Q(4).

proof.text:
The generic identity $\operatorname{Spec}L	o H_L\simeq N_L$ gives a commutative square with right side $
u:N	o H$ and bottom $e_H:S	o H$. The morphism $
u$ is finite by hypothesis, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and separated. A DVR is a valuation ring, as recorded in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Therefore [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension] supplies a unique lift $e_N:S	o N$ of this square. It restricts to the generic identity and satisfies $
u e_N=e_H$. Finiteness is used here, whereas the component-dominant normalization property alone would not apply to $e_H$.

source.place: Appendix A.4 proof, identity lifts by finiteness. Stacks: proper valuative criterion and finite morphisms are proper.

proof.text: The target $N$ is separated over $S$ by hypothesis. Step 1 gives schematic density of the generic fibres in $S,N,N^2,N^3$ (only $N,N^3$ are needed for the group identities). The two associativity maps $N^3\to N$ agree generically by step 3; the left and right unit maps $N\to N$ agree with the identity generically by step 7; and the two inverse-product maps $N\to N$ agree generically with $e_N$ composed with the structure map. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] to each pair over $S$. This proves all group diagrams. The equations in steps 6 and 7 make $\nu$ a homomorphism, and its generic identification is the one in step 3. For uniqueness, any other such group structure has these same generic multiplication, inverse and identity, because $\nu_L$ is an isomorphism. Apply the same separated-target lemma on $N^2,N,S$ to compare the three operations. They are equal, proving uniqueness.
